answers.reasoning: Mean latency does not bound tail latency; reliable delivery alone does not establish an end-to-end deadline.
Reusable middleware/components do not justify reusing sensor calibrations, transforms or environmental settings unchecked.
The actual screenshot is a generic empty simulation scene, not a completed model editor or quantitative calibration experiment.
The neighboring model editor page explicitly generates individual SDF models; the diagram comparison is not an exclusive grammar restriction.
The curved arrow visibly returns back-end information to the front end rather than carrying raw sensor data or forward constraints.
The source restarts a simulator without specifying previous-instance handling; explicitly choosing reuse or stop/restart avoids ungrounded automatic attachment assumptions.
The actual enlarged still shows navigation active, localization active and feedback reached; it does not merely display readiness or an ongoing remaining-distance state.

Run A exhausted the stipulated recovery/replan with no feasible path and should report goal failure; Run B needs a valid time-consistent transform and localization state before motion. Neither goal acceptance nor a static map legitimizes unsafe continuation.
The actual slide says Data Distribution System, while the official OMG standard title is Data Distribution Service; ROS2 is middleware, not an OS kernel.
Sensor observations flow from simulation to ROS consumers, and velocity commands flow from ROS controller to simulated drive. The illustrative topic names and compatibility premises are explicit.
